title: Minimum Distance to Type a Word Using Two Fingers
summary: Given a string, calculate the minimum total distance to type it using two fingers on a keyboard layout where each letter's position is defined by coordinates.
statement: Given a string, calculate the minimum total distance to type it using two fingers on a keyboard layout where each letter's position is defined by coordinates. The distance between any two points is the sum of the absolute differences in their x and y coordinates. The initial positions of the fingers are free and do not contribute to the distance.
constraints: word contains two to three hundred uppercase letters on the six-column alphabet keyboard.
Moving a finger costs Manhattan distance; either finger may start anywhere for free.
Type letters in order and return the minimum total movement of two fingers.
hints: A state is the pair of letters currently occupied by the two fingers.
Both initial positions are unplaced, making their first movement cost zero.
For each next letter, transition by moving either the left or right finger and retain the cheapest duplicate state.
Every assignment of typed letters to the two fingers corresponds to exactly one transition sequence.
editorial: Dynamic programming maps the two current finger positions to minimum cost after each typed prefix. For the next letter, move either finger and merge identical resulting states by minimum. A sentinel position has zero distance to any first letter. The oracle independently enumerates all 2^n finger-choice sequences on seeded short words.

tests.explanation: One finger types C then K for distance two, while the other types A then E for distance one.
An optimal division of letters between the fingers costs six.
